## Tumbao {#congas-tumbao}

*For congas, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one conga part the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Tumbao**. It is built up from 3 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The basic conga part, on one drum with the hands alternating: left-hand heel on 1, left-hand toe on the and of 1, a right-hand slap on 2, left toe on the and of 2, left heel on 3, left toe on the and of 3, then two right-hand open tones on 4 and the and of 4. Heel and toe are quiet; slap and open tones carry.

It belongs in *Son montuno*, *Cha-cha* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the cha-cha style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"congas":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)

Start with something simpler. Only the two right-hand open tones of the tumbao, on 4 and the and of 4. The first thing to play.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas.qmd#congas-opens) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)","opts":{"congas":"opens"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)

The right hand of the tumbao by itself: a slap on 2, then open tones on 4 and the and of 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas.qmd#congas-slapopen) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)","opts":{"congas":"slapopen"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3)

The left hand of the tumbao by itself: heel on 1, toe on the and of 1, toe on the and of 2, heel on 3, toe on the and of 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas.qmd#congas-heeltoe) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3)","opts":{"congas":"heeltoe"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Tumbao, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Both hands: heel, toe, slap, toe, heel, toe, open, open. Heel and toe quiet; slap and open tones carry.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"congas":"tumbao"}},{"label":"Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"congas":"heeltoe"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's congas off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"congas":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

## Tumbao, two drums {#congas-tumbao2}

*For congas, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one conga part the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Tumbao, two drums**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The tumbao in the first bar. In the second, the right hand plays two open tones on the lower drum, on the and of 2 and on 3, in place of the toe and the heel; then the left-hand toe and the two open tones of beat 4 on the higher drum. The low drum belongs to the bar with three clave notes, which is the second bar of the 2-3 clave.

It belongs in *Son montuno*, *Cha-cha* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the son montuno style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao, two drums","opts":{"congas":"tumbao2"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Tumbao

Start with something simpler. The basic conga part, on one drum with the hands alternating: left-hand heel on 1, left-hand toe on the and of 1, a right-hand slap on 2, left toe on the and of 2, left heel on 3, left toe on the and of 3, then two right-hand open tones on 4 and the and of 4. Heel and toe are quiet; slap and open tones carry.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"congas":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Tumbao, two drums, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The tumbao, then in the second bar the right hand moves to the lower drum for two open tones on the and of 2 and on 3, then back up.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao, two drums","opts":{"congas":"tumbao2"}},{"label":"Tumbao (the step before)","opts":{"congas":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 100 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's congas off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao, two drums","opts":{"congas":"tumbao2"}}]'></div>

- **Plays with, in cha-cha:** [Cha-cha](bass.qmd#bass-chacha) (bass line), [Cha-cha](chords.qmd#chords-chacha) (comping rhythm), [Cha-cha](drums.qmd#drums-chacha) (drum groove).
- **Other conga parts in the Latin group:** [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao), [Tumbao, two drums](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao2), [Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)](congas.qmd#congas-opens), [Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)](congas.qmd#congas-slapopen).

## Steady congas {#congas-steady}

*For congas, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one conga part the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Steady congas**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A quiet part that suits any music: open tones on 4 and the and of 4, a slap on 2, and a light heel and toe between. In 3/4: heel toe on 1, slap toe on 2, two open tones on 3. In 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8: heel, toe, toe on each beat, the slap on beat 2 and two open tones to finish the bar.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boogaloo*, *Stride piano*, *Boogie-woogie*, *Ragtime*, *Jump blues*, *Bossa nova*, *Son montuno*, *Cha-cha*, *Tango*, *Calypso*, *Ska / reggae*, *Reggaeton*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Emo / pop-punk*, *Acoustic strum*, *Piano ballad*, *Dance pop*, *Motown / soul*, *12/8 doo-wop*, *Country train beat*, *Boom-chick*, *Freylekhs / polka*, *John Prine Fingerpicking*, *Waltz (in one)*, *Hymn (four parts)* and *Folk carol*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Steady congas","opts":{"congas":"steady"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)

Start with something simpler. Only the two right-hand open tones of the tumbao, on 4 and the and of 4. The first thing to play.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas.qmd#congas-opens) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)","opts":{"congas":"opens"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)

The right hand of the tumbao by itself: a slap on 2, then open tones on 4 and the and of 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas.qmd#congas-slapopen) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)","opts":{"congas":"slapopen"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Steady congas, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A quiet part that suits anything: slap on 2, open tones on 4 and the and of 4, light heel and toe between.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Steady congas","opts":{"congas":"steady"}},{"label":"Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2) (the step before)","opts":{"congas":"slapopen"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's congas off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Steady congas","opts":{"congas":"steady"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Steady congas","opts":{"congas":"steady"}}]'></div>
